description: Bounded public disposition for the ROCm/HIP host-KV block-reuse proof: physical host read at the link roof with logical service scaling with query-row reuse (pinned arm 13.997 to 244.944 GB/s logical across K=1..96; registered-pageable arm 14.02/112.04/143.94/246.89 at K=1/8/32/96), exact-attention parity at rel_rms 4.5e-6..4.96e-6 with max_abs <= 2.3935e-7, the compute crossover above K=16 explained by an f32 kernel, and the registered-host-memory prerequisite with its page-fault error. The executing runtime tree, model weights, container bytes, and raw receipts are excluded from publication; values below are sanitized summaries of campaign-local receipts.
model_name: Qwen3.8-27B attention geometry (16 full-attention layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, GQA 6)
model_revision: geometry from the campaign artifact; no weight payload is part of this repository
model_download_source: public artifact exists; no weight payload or container byte is part of this repository
prompt: not applicable; the instrument is a kernel microbenchmark over a fixed KV geometry
warmup: event-timed passes; medians of repeated runs

expected_range.pageable_raw: kernel page fault: Page not present or supervisor privilege

tolerance.physical_gbps: repeat runs reproduce the K<=8 plateau within ~2%, K=32 within ~10%
tolerance.parity: vs a VRAM fp32 reference with a different loop order and softmax formulation

known_limitations: The two arms disagree at K>=32 (4.50 vs 5.770 GB/s physical); they must not be averaged.
The JSON receipt for the registered-pageable arm is absent from disk; only the run log survives.
No llama.cpp integration, no real model tensors, no GQA head sharing, and no end-to-end tokens/s.
Each byte is read once by construction plus rate agreement, not by a hardware page counter.
Logical bandwidth is block reuse, not physical link bandwidth.
